lines.text: Yarrow helps you write the right ticket, gets an agent to build it, and lets you review what it ships. All in one place. Let me show you.
I sign in with GitHub, and here's my dashboard. Tickets come from GitHub issues, Jira, Linear or Trello. None yet, so let's write one.
I want a new functionality for my application. Right now, all the to-dos are mixed up, and you can't filter them by status. So I need buttons above the list: All, To Do, Doing and Done.
Seconds later, I have a clear ticket, with its acceptance criteria. I create it.
It's in To do. I slide to start.
Muse Wonder, Meta's model, picks it up in the cloud. It reads the code, writes the change, runs the app, and records a demo.
Eight minutes later, it's ready to review, with a live demo. Let's watch.
Wait, can I ask a question?
Can you click on the Doing button, and then add a new task?
Okay, I see. I think it would be interesting to add a new ticket, to set the status of a task while we're creating it. What do you think?
And there's my next ticket, straight from the conversation. Create ticket.
This one, I've seen it work, and I know what changed. I slide to merge.
Merged. And my new ticket is already waiting in To do.
That's Yarrow. Try it on yarrow dot run.
